1.title: Helm, Kustomize, CRDs and Operators
1.text: Welcome to Module four: Helm, Kustomize, C R Ds and Operators. It covers the exam area Cluster Architecture, Installation and Configuration. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, and every task was run on a real cluster, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Use Helm and Kustomize to install cluster components. Understand C R Ds (Custom Resource Definitions), install and configure operators. Practice with six hands-on labs worth thirty-seven points.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Cluster Architecture, Installation and Configuration (twenty-five percent). Practice in this module: six labs, thirty-seven points, about thirty-nine minutes. Exam format: performance-based tasks in a live terminal, scored on the final cluster state. Validated on: Kubernetes version one point thirty-seven point zero.

1.title: Helm in one page
1.text: Helm in one page. Helm is the package manager for Kubernetes. A chart is a package of templated manifests. A release is one installation of a chart in a cluster. Values ( values dot yaml plus your overrides) fill the templates. Every install, upgrade and rollback creates a new revision. Exam tip: Always pass dash n namespace to Helm commands, or you work in the default namespace.

1.title: Helm in one page, continued
1.text: Helm in one page. Add a repository. helm repo add name url then helm repo update. Search a repository. helm search repo word (add the versions flag for all chart versions). See default values. helm show values chart. Install. helm install release chart dash n ns the create namespace flag the set flag key val. Install from a values file. helm install release chart dash f myvalues dot yaml. List releases. helm list dash n ns ( dash A for all namespaces). Upgrade. helm upgrade release chart dash n ns the set flag key val.

1.title: Helm in one page, continued
1.text: Helm in one page. History. helm history release dash n ns. Roll back. helm rollback release revision dash n ns. Remove. helm uninstall release dash n ns. Render without installing. helm template release chart the set flag key val. Values you supplied. helm get values release ( the all flag adds chart defaults). The manifests in the cluster. helm get manifest release. Facts that are tested. the set flag overrides one value ( the set flag replica Count three ); nested keys use dots ( service dot port eighty eighty ). Never edit the chart to change a value.

1.title: Helm in one page, continued
1.text: Helm in one page. A rollback is a new revision. After upgrade (revision two) and rollback one, helm history shows revision three with the description "Rollback to one" (Lab four point two). Release names are namespaced. Always pass dash n for a release that is not in the current namespace; helm list shows only the current namespace. helm template and helm install the dry run flag show output and create nothing. Naming: in a chart made by helm create webapp, the Deployment is named release -webapp.

1.title: Kustomize in one page
1.text: Kustomize in one page. Kustomize customizes plain yamel without templates. It is built into kube control: kube control customize dir prints the result, kube control apply dash k dir applies it. A directory with a customization dot yaml is a base; an overlay points to a base and changes it. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: kube control apply dash k dir applies a customization and kube control customize dir only previews it.

1.title: Kustomize in one page, continued
1.text: Kustomize in one page. resources. the base directories or files to include. namespace, name Prefix, name Suffix, common Labels. applied to all objects. replicas. change the replica count of a named workload. images. change image name or tag. patches. strategic-merge or Jason patches for anything else. config Map Generator, secret Generator. make Config Maps and Secrets (with a name hash). Workflow: write the overlay, run kube control customize to look at the output first, create the namespace if it does not exist (Kustomize does not create it), then kube control apply dash k. The base stays unchanged (Lab four point five).

1.title: Helm or Kustomize?
1.text: Helm or Kustomize? Idea. Helm: templates plus values, versioned releases. Kustomize: patches on plain yamel. Rollback. Helm: helm rollback. Kustomize: none (use git). Typical exam task. Helm: install a chart, upgrade, roll back, set a value. Kustomize: build an overlay.

1.title: CRDs
1.text: C R Ds. A Custom Resource Definition (C R D) teaches the A P I server a new resource type. After the C R D (Custom Resource Definition) is installed, you can create custom resources (C R s) of that kind like any object. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: Wait until the C R D is Established before you create objects of its kind.

1.title: CRDs, continued
1.text: C R Ds. The C R D metadata dot name must be plural. group. Wait until it is Established: kube control wait the for flag set to condition Established crd or name. Then: kube control get crontabs, kube control get ct, kube control explain crontab dot spec. With a schema, the A P I server rejects fields it does not know (the object fails validation). Find C R Ds: kube control get crd; the A P I group of a resource: kube control api resources.

1.title: Operators
1.text: Operators. An operator is a controller plus its C R Ds that automates running an application (install, backup, upgrade, failover). You install the operator (often with Helm or a manifest), then you create a custom resource that states what you want, and the operator makes it so. On the exam you install an operator the way the task says (Helm chart or manifest), create or edit its custom resource, and check the result. Troubleshooting an operator is troubleshooting its Pod: kube control dash n ns logs deploy or operator.

1.title: Lab 4.1: helm install
1.text: Lab four point one: helm install. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. A Helm chart exists in the directory about slash charts slash webapp. Install it as the release shop in the namespace helm ns (create the namespace if needed) with two replicas, by overriding the chart value replica Count on the command line (do not edit the chart). Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

1.title: Lab 4.1: helm install, Solution
1.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run helm install shop about slash charts slash webapp dash n helm ns the create namespace flag the set flag replica Count two the wait flag the timeout flag one hundred twenty seconds. Then helm list dash n helm ns. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

1.title: Lab 4.2: helm upgrade rollback
1.text: Lab four point two: helm upgrade rollback. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about seven minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. The release app (chart about slash charts slash webapp ) is installed in the namespace helm ns with one replica. First upgrade the release so that it runs three replicas. Then the change turns out to be a mistake: roll the release back to its first revision. At the end the release must run one replica and the history must show the upgrade and the rollback. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 4.2: helm upgrade rollback, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run helm upgrade app about slash charts slash webapp dash n helm ns the set flag replica Count three the wait flag the timeout flag one hundred twenty seconds. Then helm history app dash n helm ns. Then helm rollback app one dash n helm ns the wait flag the timeout flag one hundred twenty seconds. Then helm history app dash n helm ns. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 4.3: helm values uninstall
2.text: Lab four point three: helm values uninstall. This task is worth six points, and you should plan about six minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Two releases exist in the namespace helm ns: old and keep. Remove the release old completely. Save the user-supplied values of the release keep (not the chart defaults) to the file about slash answers slash keep values dot yaml. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 4.3: helm values uninstall, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run helm list dash n helm ns. Then helm uninstall old dash n helm ns. Then helm get values keep dash n helm ns about slash answers slash keep values dot yaml. Then cat about slash answers slash keep values dot yaml. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 4.4: helm template
2.text: Lab four point four: helm template. This task is worth four points, and you should plan about four minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. Without installing anything, render the manifests of the chart about slash charts slash webapp for a release named preview with four replicas and save the output to about slash answers slash rendered dot yaml. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 4.4: helm template, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run helm template preview about slash charts slash webapp the set flag replica Count four about slash answers slash rendered dot yaml. Then grep dash E replicas then pipe to name preview about slash answers slash rendered dot yaml. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 4.5: kustomize overlay
2.text: Lab four point five: customize overlay. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. A Kustomize base exists in about slash kust slash base (a Deployment web with one replica and a Service web ). Create an overlay in about slash kust slash overlays slash prod that reuses the base and changes: namespace prod, a name prefix prod-, three replicas, and the container image to engine X stable alpine. Do not edit the base. Create the namespace prod, then apply the overlay to the cluster. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 4.5: kustomize overlay, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. cat about slash kust slash overlays slash prod slash customization dot yaml. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control customize about slash kust slash overlays slash prod then pipe to head -thirty. Then kube control create ns prod. Then kube control apply dash k about slash kust slash overlays slash prod. Then kube control dash n prod rollout status deployment prod web the timeout flag set to one hundred twenty seconds. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Lab 4.6: crd custom resource
2.text: Lab four point six: crd custom resource. This task is worth seven points, and you should plan about eight minutes. Start by switching to the kind-C K A context. The file about slash crd slash crontab crd dot yaml defines a Custom Resource Definition for the kind Cron Tab (group stable dot example dot com ). Install it in the cluster. Then create a Cron Tab custom resource named nightly in the namespace default with spec dot cron Spec zero two and spec dot image backup one dot zero. Finally write the full name of the C R D (the value in the N A M E column of kube control get crd ) to about slash answers slash crd name dot txt. Pause the video and try the task yourself, then come back for the solution.

2.title: Lab 4.6: crd custom resource, Solution
2.text: Here is one way to solve it. Run kube control apply dash f about slash crd slash crontab crd dot yaml. Then kube control wait the for flag set to condition Established crd slash crontabs dot stable dot example dot com the timeout flag set to sixty seconds. kube control apply dash f -. The manifest comes next, as shown on the screen. Then kube control get crd then pipe to grep crontabs. Then echo crontabs dot stable dot example dot com about slash answers slash crd name dot txt. Then check the result with a read command, the way you would on the exam.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the difference between a chart and a release? Answer: A chart is the package; a release is one installation of it in a cluster. Question two. How do you change one chart value at install time without editing the chart? Answer: the set flag key value (or dash f values dot yaml ). Question three. After helm upgrade and helm rollback one, how many revisions exist? Answer: Three; the rollback is a new revision.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which command shows only the values the user supplied? Answer: helm get values release (without the all flag ). Question five. How do you preview manifests without touching the cluster? Answer: helm template, or kube control customize for Kustomize. Question six. Does Kustomize create the target namespace? Answer: No; create it first.

2.title: Recall Check 3
2.text: Recall check three. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question seven. What must a C R D's metadata dot name look like? Answer: plural. group. Question eight. What is an operator? Answer: A controller with C R Ds that automates managing an application.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Helm lifecycle: install, upgrade, history, rollback, uninstall; dash n always. Values: the set flag, dash f, helm get values, helm show values. Preview: helm template, kube control customize. Kustomize: kube control apply dash k; resources, namespace, name Prefix, replicas, images, patches. C R D: name plural. group, wait for Established, then create C R s. Operator: controller plus C R D; installed via Helm or manifest. In the next module, we continue the course.
